doc.title: Joe Temperley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

chapter: Recordings and the Buck Clayton band
title: Favourite recordings and the Dave McKenna duet
summary: He liked his duet with Dave McKenna and says he rarely listens to his own records.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: What was your favorite recent recording of yours? I know you did a “Concerto for Joe,” not your most recent though.
But it was done in too much of a hurry to be my favorite. I liked the one I did with Dave McKenna, that turned out good.

The duet, yeah. I love playing with Dave McKenna. I mean that’s another one who sets a distinctive style. Nobody can play that rhythmic pulse like he can. That’s another thing that’s a bygone thing. But you know I’m always looking, the next record, maybe the next record will be the one. I don’t tend to listen to the records I’ve made particularly. I hear it a couple of times and I say oh yeah, okay. I could have done this or I could have done that or this could have been better. So it always can be better. And I feel that if you feel like that it always will be better. I think it’s important to just keep forging ahead.
Yeah. To not do one recording and think that that’s the best you can do.
